Rows 1-2 are a light red 1-2 row highlight along the top of the backrest, with no front-edge line or eave shadow beneath it. Rows 3-10 are a vertical red back face with a gold plate at rows 5-6 and a darker lower band at rows 9-10. The width profile (36 at rows 1-3, then 44-46 from row 4) comes from the armrests and the backrest body, with no widen-then-narrow ellipse. The seat cushion is hidden behind the backrest, so no horizontal seat surface is visible from above. This matches the 'seat: band 2' and 'front elevation' wrong examples rather than the right seat example, which has a top of about 5 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small row of three red seats seen from behind. It has about 3 red lightness steps (a highlight on the top edge, a mid red, a dark red) plus a dark base, against roughly 5-6 steps on the references (hedge, well, stall). The measured facts back this up: 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black line around every seat. That is the sticker look, and it is unlike the tinted dark-material outlines of the hedge (0%), the stall (1%) and the well (33%). The only reference at 100% is the thin lamp, which is a sparse object. Colour count is low at 12 distinct colours, compared with 38-40 on the large references and 11-14 on the small ones. The 12-colour median per tile is comparable to the hedge's 10, and there are no 5x5 flat fills, so density is only slightly lower. The backs have little grain or texture beyond a highlight line and a few shading dots. Shading is shallow and the outline is black rather than a dark red-brown, so a careful artist would not accept it next to the references.
